items.title: John Batiste "Bat" Mosley Interview, 1961-09-23
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Fess of course, he's older than you and his memory goes back and forth. He told us about places over like on Brooklyn Street, the ping pong. Do you remember that old place? Yeah, and that's what they called the hunky-tonk.

ctx.x: worked mostly in? Oh yeah, the most they played was in Yawlin. Well you take all the bands from that time, the most they played was in Yawlin. One time we played over here, one of those halls, you know society would give a dance, you see. I like to take like SP out there, used to pay off like twice a month, you see. Well every time the SP, because they had a lot of people waiting, every time they would pay off or they'd have a dance here. I had a place right there, Precious Ranch used to be right here, several…

Fess of course, he's older than you and his memory goes back and forth. He told us about places over like on Brooklyn Street, the ping pong. Do you remember that old place? Yeah, and that's what they called the hunky-tonk.

Then they had another place out here on Wilmore in Brooklyn, with the green tree. That was called the hunky-tonk too. Then they had another place out here on Tash and Bringer, right by the bridge out there, right on evening. They had a place that was called the hunky-tonk. But I'll tell you, the most of those places used to have pianos, you know. Those old-time pianos, those rollers. Well they used that, you see. They couldn't afford, you know, green at that time and high bands. Most bands would play over here…
